output.patientMessage: Go to an emergency department now — today, not tomorrow. New trouble controlling your bladder plus numbness between your legs after a back injury can mean nerve compression at the base of the spine, which needs urgent scanning and specialist assessment. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself. If you develop leg weakness, can't walk, or can't pass urine at all, call 911.

anchors.quote:
**Neurological Emergency (minutes-to-hours matter):**
- **Saddle anesthesia** — perineal numbness (S2-S5); test with pinprick bilaterally
- **Urinary retention or new incontinence** — bladder scan for post-void residual (PVR); PVR > 200 mL is abnormal
MRI is the only appropriate emergent study. CT myelogram is the fallback if MRI is unavailable.
Delay in diagnosis results in permanent deficits.
